# What these three steps were for

The manuscript-readiness review (`reports/manuscript_plan.html`) listed eight gaps. Three are
closed here, and none of them closed the way the review expected.

<div class="verdict-mid">
**G1 (steps 24 and 24b) — the better cell labels OVERTURN a headline, and the control confirms
it.** The two callers agree on only **70.2%** of cells. Step 16's claim that RB1 "sits at
chance" does not survive: at matched cell counts RB1's fraction-at-chance is **0.818**
(step-16 labels) against **0.535** (step-19 labels), and the same pair sits further from chance
under step-19 labels in **80.3%** of comparisons (*p* = 2.9e-39). This is a correction, not a
flag.

**G4 (step 22) — ligand-receptor co-expression in proximity is measurable and small.** The
effects are 1.01-1.18 fold and reach significance only where field-of-view counts run to the
hundreds. The one large-looking checkpoint number is exactly the shape transcript leakage
produces, which is what the distance-band discriminator was built to catch.

**G5 (step 23) — 9p24.1 dosage evidence is NOT obtained, because the negative control fires.**
The score does rise in IB1's hotspots, in the 99th percentile of all cytobands, with the
non-immune genes rising too. But the identical statistic is also significant in RB1, which has
no Hodgkin component, and the signal is spread across unrelated lineages rather than confined
to one clone. Both facts point away from dosage.
</div>

# G1 — do the better cell labels change the architecture result?

Every cell-type-conditioned result in steps 16 and 17 reads
`output/16_celltypes/cell_celltypes.csv.gz`. Step 24 re-runs the identical permutation
statistic — mean count of type-B neighbours within 20 um of a type-A cell, labels permuted
within local-density deciles — twice on the same cells and the same regions, once per label
source.

<div class="verdict-no">
**What is not re-testable, and it is not a limitation of this step.** Step 16's headline numbers
are about **Tfh**: self-aggregation 2.74x, Tfh-B 1.62x, Tfh-macrophage 0.47x. **Step 19 has no
Tfh label by design** — cluster-based T-cell subsetting failed three ways and is a closed
avenue, so T stays one label and Tfh comes only from per-cell argmax subsets, which is what
step 16 already does. The Tfh findings, and step 16's Tfh composition result, therefore cannot
be re-derived here at all. Claiming they were "confirmed" would be false.
</div>

```{r g1-agree}
kb(LA, caption = "Agreement between the two callers, on cells named by both")
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**Agreement is 70.2% overall and worst where the lineage is rare** — NK 32.1%, plasma cell
37.5%, against B at 77.7%. Architecture enrichments nonetheless correlate at Spearman
**0.792** with 79.1% sign agreement across the 297 (region x pair) cells testable under both.
</div>

```{r g1-chance}
kb(CF, caption = "Fraction of cell-type pairs sitting at chance (q >= 0.05), by label source")
kb(SG[, .(samp, bin_region, labels, pairs, med_enrich, n_sig)],
   caption = "Lymphoid <-> myeloid segregation under each label source")
```

<div class="verdict-no">
**R9's direction survives; the RB1 claim does not.** Lymphoid/myeloid segregation is present in
IB1 under both label sets, and RB1 remains less structured than IB1. But step 16 reported RB1
as essentially all at chance, 0.93–1.09, and that is wrong.
</div>

## The control: labels, or statistical power?

Step 19 names about twice as many cells as the step-16 argmax leaves named, and more labelled
cells buys power on its own. Step 24b removes that confound: for every region and every shared
cell type it down-samples **both** sources to `min(n16, n19)`, so `n_a` and `n_b` are identical
for every pair by construction. The matching runs in both directions on purpose — step 19 names
~1.24× as many B cells but only ~0.45× as many T cells, because step 16's T count is the sum of
its four T subsets, so a one-directional control would have been wrong. Down-sampling removes
**labels, never cells**, and the neighbour graph and density deciles are built once per region
from all cells present, which also fixes a second confound: step 24 subset to labelled cells
before building the graph, so the two sources saw different geometries.

```{r g1-ctl}
kb(CEF, caption = "PRIMARY, threshold-free: median |log2 enrichment| — how far the enrichments sit from chance")
kb(CPD, caption = "PAIRED, matched n: is the SAME pair further from chance under step-19 labels?")
kb(CTL, caption = "Fraction of pairs at chance. Reported for comparability with step 24, but it is thresholded and its q depends on how many pairs pile up at the permutation floor.")
```

<div class="verdict-ok">
**The labels carry it, not power.** Matching every type in every region leaves RB1 at
**0.818 vs 0.535** — the gap does not close, it slightly widens against the unmatched
0.776/0.503. Threshold-free, RB1's median |log2 enrichment| is **0.0594 vs 0.1276**, so the
step-19 labels put the enrichments **2.15× further from chance at matched n**. Paired per
(region × pair × seed), the same pair is further from chance under step-19 labels in **80.3%**
of 441 comparisons (median +0.081 log2, sign test *p* = 2.9 × 10⁻³⁹).

**Why matching did not help step 16:** at matched n its own number gets *worse*
(0.776 → 0.818) while step 19's barely moves (0.503 → 0.535). The step-19 labels are more
informative per cell, not merely more numerous. **Step 16 measured the argmax caller's silence,
not RB1's architecture.**
</div>

<div class="verdict-mid">
**IB1 is where the labels matter least**, and that is reassuring for the original result:
matched, its fraction-at-chance is 0.705 vs 0.693, a difference of 0.012. Threshold-free it
still moves (0.1751 → 0.2646), but IB1's segregation was real under either caller.
</div>

# G4 — ligand-receptor co-expression in proximity

<div class="verdict-mid">
**The words matter.** This measures **co-expression in proximity**: the rate at which a cell
within a distance band of a ligand-positive cell is receptor-positive. It is **not** signalling,
engagement or communication. Step 17 built three nulls for transcript-level PD-1/PD-L1
proximity, all three failed their own positive control, and the readout was withdrawn under a
pre-committed stopping rule. Spatial engagement of a receptor-ligand axis remains **unmeasured**
in this project.
</div>

<details>
<summary>The null is closed-form, which is the only reason the step is affordable</summary>
The first version permuted positivity 300 times per pair per band per region: 2,315 curated
pairs x 5 bands x 7 regions, i.e. ~24 million permutation evaluations over million-element
neighbour lists. Unnecessary — with A the band's sparse adjacency and P the gene-by-cell
positivity matrix, `OBS = P A P^T / sum(A)`, and under permutation within strata
`EXP = Pbar (S A S^T) Pbar^T / sum(A)` where `S A S^T` is a tiny stratum-by-stratum matrix.
Both are exact and the whole 1,125-gene square comes out in seconds. Strata are **depth decile
x cell type**: depth because positivity tracks it at AUC ~0.70 for every gene on this platform,
cell type because lineages cluster spatially and a pair expressed within one lineage would
otherwise show enrichment from lineage clustering alone.
</details>

```{r g4-hits}
if (!is.null(T1)) kb(T1[q < 0.05 & enrich_fov > 1][order(-enrich_fov)][
  , .(samp, bin_region, ligand, receptor, band, fovs, enrich_fov = round(enrich_fov,3),
      lo = round(lo,2), hi = round(hi,2), q = signif(q,3))],
  caption = "Every Tier 1 pair significantly ENRICHED, FOV cluster bootstrap")
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**The signals are real, coherent and small.** *CXCL13*-*CXCR5* — the Tfh/B follicular axis — is
the strongest and the only one enriched across **all four** distance bands in IB1 background
(1.14, 1.16, 1.15, 1.13), so it cannot be a segmentation-boundary effect. The stromal
*CCL19*/*CCL21*-*CCR7* axis follows at 1.01-1.07. The declared Hodgkin axis
*CCL17*/*CCL22*-*CCR4* reaches only 1.055 and 1.075, in IB1 **background**.

Note what carries significance: every hit sits in a region with hundreds of fields of view.
IB1's hotspots (16 FOVs) and FL foci (25) produce nothing significant, which is the same
power wall step 21 hit.
</div>

<div class="verdict-no">
**The most eye-catching number is the one to distrust, and the discriminator says so.**
*PDCD1LG2*-*PDCD1* in IB1's FL foci reaches enrichment **2.28** in the 0-10 um band — the
largest Tier 1 value anywhere. Across the bands it runs **2.28 -> 1.54 -> 1.14 -> 1.01**: a
monotone decay to nothing by 40-80 um, on 25 FOVs, with a 95% interval of [1.00, 4.96] and
*q* = 0.167. That is precisely the profile transcript leakage produces — step 18 measured
marker transcripts displaced toward marker-rich neighbours — and precisely why the distance-band
profile is part of the design rather than an afterthought. It is **not** reported as an
observation about the checkpoint axis.

Note also that *CCL17*/*CCL22*-*CCR4* is **below** 1 inside the FL foci (0.93, 0.86 at 40-80 um),
the opposite of what a cell-pair reading of step 16's CCR4 gradient would predict. The gradient
is a regional association, not a pairwise one.
</div>

```{r g4-shape}
if (!is.null(PRF)) kb(PRF[, .N, by = .(tier, shape)][order(tier, -N)],
  caption = "Leakage-shape classification. Tier 2 is a screen and carries no p-value.")
```

# G5 — is there dosage evidence for 9p24.1 gain?

Step 17's strongest within-sample result is ligand-side checkpoint elevation in IB1's hotspots
with interferon flat, which is the pattern 9p24.1 copy gain predicts. Its 9p24.1 module was
*CD274* + *PDCD1LG2* + *JAK2* — all three immune-inducible, so RNA could not separate gain from
induction. Installing `org.Hs.eg.db` showed the panel carries **nine** 9p24.1 genes, five of them
(*CDC37L1*, *ERMP1*, *KDM4C*, *MLANA*, *PLPP6*) not immune-functional. Copy gain is indifferent
to gene function and raises all of them; interferon raises only the immune ones. The null is
every other cytoband measured on the same panel in the same cells — 440-443 bands with at least
five detected genes.

```{r g5-rank}
if (!is.null(DS)) kb(DS[, .(contrast, celltype, fovs_a, bands_in_null,
   score_all = round(score_all,3), rank = paste0(rank_of,"/",bands_in_null),
   top_pct = pct_of_bands)], caption = "9p24.1 band score against the whole-genome band null")
```

```{r g5-disc}
if (!is.null(DS)) kb(DS[, .(contrast, celltype, n_immune, immune = round(score_immune,3),
   n_clean, clean = round(score_clean,3), lo = round(clean_lo,2), hi = round(clean_hi,2),
   q = signif(q_clean,3), verdict)],
   caption = "The discriminator: immune vs non-immune genes on the same band")
```

<div class="verdict-no">
**The negative control fires, and that settles it.** RB1 is the pure-FL recurrence; 9p24.1 gain
is a classic-Hodgkin lesion and should be absent there, which makes RB1 the
construction-identical control the project uses everywhere else. The clean-subset score is
significantly elevated in **RB1's fibroblasts** (0.195, *q* = 0.039). A statistic that fires
where the lesion cannot be is not measuring the lesion.

**And the signal is not confined, which a clonal event must be.** In IB1's hotspots the score
is up in three of four lineages and significant in two — T cells (0.480, *q* = 0.039) and
fibroblasts (0.795, *q* = 0.039) — while flat in myeloid and negative in B. Copy gain belongs
to a clone. Bystander T cells and fibroblasts in a hotspot are not the clone, so a score rising
across unrelated lineages is leakage- or gradient-shaped.
</div>

```{r g5-conf}
if (!is.null(CN)) kb(CN, caption = "Confinement: how many lineages carry the signal")
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**What survives.** IB1's hotspots do carry an elevated 9p24.1 neighbourhood — rank 5 of 439 in
T cells and 5 of 443 in fibroblasts, the 99th percentile of all cytobands — and the non-immune
genes rise more than the immune ones. Read as a regional expression gradient over a chromosomal
neighbourhood, that is a real observation. Read as copy number, it fails both of its own checks.
**Step 17's 9p24.1 module stays EXPLORATORY, and this step is the reason it should not be
upgraded.**

The verdict column in `dosage_9p24.csv` is control-aware: an earlier version did not consult
RB1 and labelled RB1's own fibroblasts "DOSAGE-CONSISTENT".
</div>

```{r g5-genes}
if (!is.null(DG)) kb(DG[grepl("hotspot", contrast) & celltype %in% c("T","fibro")][
  order(celltype, class, -lfc)], caption = "Per-gene detail, IB1 hotspot, the two significant lineages")
```

# What these steps cannot support

- **A confirmation of step 16's Tfh architecture findings.** Not re-testable: step 19 has no
  Tfh label by design.
- **A claim that RB1 is spatially structured to the same degree as IB1.** RB1 is less
  structured than IB1 under both callers; what is corrected is only that it is not
  *unstructured*.
- **Any statement that a ligand-receptor axis is engaged, active, or signalling.** Only
  co-expression in proximity is measured, and spatial engagement remains withdrawn from step 17.
- **A p-value for any Tier 2 ligand-receptor pair.** Tier 2 is a screen with no bootstrap.
- **9p24.1 copy gain, in any cell type or region.** The control fires and the signal is not
  confined.
- **Anything cross-sample.** Every contrast here is within one sample.
